lines.english: "…Haah."
After taking a hot morning shower, my body finally adjusts itself to the cold winter air.
It's a bit cold, but the weather outside is nice.
From the buzzing of the washing machine to the rays of sunlight streaming through the window, everything around me signals the coming of a new day.
Or perhaps "begun" is the wrong word here, because I have yet to do anything other than relax so far, but that's what Sundays are for, right?
And now, my customary Sunday battle begins.
"Setsuna."
"Wake up already."
"Mhmmm… Just a little while longer."
"It's half past ten. It's daytime already."
"You're right. It's only half past ten. It's still morning."
…That's right, a brutal battle to pinpoint where exactly morning ends and daytime begins.
"Most places will stop serving breakfast specials in 30 minutes. It's totally daytime."
"In other words, there's still 30 minutes of morning left."
"If I could actually trust you to wake up within 30 minutes, that line might've worked…"
"This is the first Sunday in ages that doesn't involve any events, shopping or strolls. I'm begging you, let me sleep a while longer…!"
My delicate princess is terrible at waking up, which incidentally makes her great at not waking up.
When she's like this, I feel like a lone traveler marching against the north wind. Ordinary means simply will not work.
Which is why I have no choice…
"Fine… Good night, Setsuna."
"Thank you, Haruki-kun. That's why I love y…"
"Right, I'll be in the kitchen making lunch. You can stay asleep as long as you want."
"Hm? Did you say something?"
Of course, the only thing capable of stopping the north wind is the sun.
"No! You can't cook, Haruki-kun… That would depreciate my role as your wife."
"We're both working adults, so what's the problem? Either way, you're clearly too tired from work right now."
"You're the last person I wanna hear that from. You always leave for work before me and come home after me…"
"I normally leave everything to you, Setsuna. Let me return the favor on Sundays at least."
"But Haruki-kun, you already do the laundry and clean the house whenever I look away.
"Then wake up. I'm starving over here! If you neglect me, I swear I'll cook something myself, you hear?"
"Ohh, you're a demon! Satan himself! The CEO of the underworld!"
"My princess, may I suggest you refrain from besmirching the name of Miss Houjou High by the means of sloth?"
And so, even as she wastes the whole day away in bed, my wife makes sure to protect her role as a working housewife.
The girl formerly known as Ogiso Setsuna. Kitahara Setsuna.
Former title holder for Miss Houjou High for three consecutive years, and now the public relations idol for Knights Records.
"Come on, keep your promise and wake up."
"…Wake me, Haruki-kun."
Setsuna stretches her arms toward me from the bed like a spoiled child…
Or more accurately, like a princess; a side she would never show to anyone else.
"Alright, alri… Uwaah!"
"Hehe, I got you."
Before I know it, her hand drags my entire body down toward her in bed.
"Now that you're down here, why don't you take a nap as well? No one will fault you for relaxing today."
"You say that, but you don't have the slightest intention of actually sleeping, do you?"
Her demeanor doesn't hint at a desire for peaceful sleep at all. There's something more aggressive and carnal in her eyes.
"Hey, hey, Haruki-kun… mhh."
To be more precise, it has something to do with how her lips are going down my neck.
"You'll just feel more hungry if you do that."
"Looks like I have a delicious lunch ahead of me then. Mh, chu…"
"…! No, it's morning. This isn't the time."
"But your thing down here… is saying it's the perfect time."
To be more precise, the way her fingers go down my…
"My thing doesn't speak… Aah…! S-Setsuna… but…"
"Mh, hehe, Haruki-kun… Mh, nhm, mmh."
"Ah, ah… For the love of… Hey…!"
"…! He, hehe… mphu…"
I've already stated this, but it's currently 10:30 AM.
It wouldn't be at all strange or rude for someone to come visit at this time of day…
"Hey, Setsuna. Wake up already!"
"…Ah, come to think of it, your mom said she was coming to visit this morning."
"No, she didn't! She said she'd come at noon! Why does she always have to be so impatient?"
…And so, our argument regarding when exactly morning ends is revived, as we both hurriedly jump out of bed.
It was late December.
A little over a year after Ogiso Setsuna ever so slightly changed her last name.
This is the story of that winter we spent together, in this apartment.
"Ehm, have some tea… Mother."
"No, it's okay… More importantly, I'm sorry Haruki-san. My daughter is such a sleepyhead."
"Oh no, she's normally very diligent. Today's her day off, that's all…"
"That's right! Don't jump in and say things better left unsaid, Mom!"
"You too, Setsuna. Don't jump into the conversation when you don't have to…"
"That's right, at least get dressed and dry your hair first. You're so bad-mannered."
"Oh, please forgive me. You see, my parents didn't teach me how to behave."
"Haha, ha…"
"I'm really sorry. Her father always pampered her so she never grew out of it."
"Oh, it's nothing… I should thank you for raising her to be selfish."
"Huh? Could it be you're one of those people who enjoy being toyed with, Haruki-san?"
"No, I didn't mean it that way… Well, I suppose I wouldn't mind that either anymore."
Setsuna's mom stares at me, more out of discomfort than confusion.
But I merely respond with a vague smile, with thoughts in my mind that would probably make her even more uncomfortable.
Thoughts that say "Thank you."
Thank you for raising Setsuna to be so selfish, kind, normal, and strong.
For they are the ones who raised her to be so resilient… even after the many times I've hurt her in the past.
For they are the ones who helped her return to the way she was, when she broke down.
It was all thanks to her father, her mother, and her younger brother.
"Still though, to think you're moving when things are already as busy as they are."
"What do you mean, Mom? Isn't it more efficient to take care of the cleanup and moving at the same time?"
"Besides, it'll also be more efficient for our new neighbors.
"Why not stay here a bit longer, though? It should be enough for the two of you."
"I seem to remember Father getting angry at me for 'forcing his daughter to live in such a cramped space' though…"
Next Saturday…
Just as Setsuna's mother says, Setsuna and I will move out the weekend before New Year's, and move into a two-room apartment five stations away.
Anyway, that's how things stand. Setsuna's mother came over today to help us prepare for the move.
"Ah, Mom! Don't put away all the utensils. What are we supposed to eat with tomorrow?"
"Make do with paper cups and paper trays. It's better than causing a commotion on the last day because you haven't packed everything."
"There's still a whole week until then! Start with the things we won't need first. Aah, not the TV! I still wanna watch it!"
"Oh shut up already. Go ahead and take care of everything yourself then, Setsuna."
"Haha…"
"I'll take care of everything myself, so you don't need to come over."
Those words had left my mouth the day before as if it was the most natural thing in the world… but to the Ogiso household, they were akin to heresy.
They'd retort with things like "you can't stay so formal forever" and "you're treating us like strangers" and "you said that before the wedding too."
On top of that, I think they said some rather absurd things as well, but let's not get into that…
They're not bad people, of course; I really care about them. But I can't help but laugh at how our worldviews remain so different even after all this time.
"…Oh? Look at this, Setsuna."
"What is it, Mom? I'm busy cleaning everything up by myself."
"Forget about that, look! This is your photo album from middle school."
"Oh, there it is! I knew I brought it over, but I couldn't find it all this time."
"You even brought your album to this tiny little apartment? No wonder it feels so cramped in here."
"…Really sorry about living in a tiny little apartment."
If I remember correctly, it was her daughter ーnot meーwho adamantly stated we should stay here until
"Oh goodness, this brings me back. Look, this is Setsuna during middle school. Look, look, Haruki-san."
"I've already seen it a thousand times."
I already know all about who her friends were, who she fell out with, and who she managed to reconcile with.
…In fact, I also uh… well… know about the soccer ace who confessed his love to her, down to his facial features.
Seriously, she didn't have to tell me about that part in such detail.
"She was so cute and obedient back then. When did she become such a stubborn girl who never listens to her parents?"
"Ah, Nagasaki! We went there on a school trip!"
"Yes, I remember very well. You had a 38 degree fever the day before the trip, right, Setsuna?"
"Exactly! Dad got mad and told me not to go on the trip."
"But you started bawling, demanding to go… Actually, come to think of it, it was around that time you started ignoring your parents' wishes."
"That's not true. My fever went down to 36 degrees the day after."
"I know you cheated with the thermometer. You didn't have it tightly under your armpit like you were supposed to, did you?"
"Oooh, did I now?"
"Come on, look at this picture. Your face is completely swollen red. It's perfect proof you were in terrible condition."
"Uwaa, I look so weird. Oh, this is so embarrassing. No, Haruki-kun, you can't look!"
"…I'm not gonna look. How about we hurry up and get this place cleaned up already?"
And with that done…
"Thank you so much for today, you were a huge help."
"Yes, but it was naive to think we'd manage it all in a single day. I'll come back next time."
"We'll both be at work until moving day. There won't be anyone home to open the door for you."
"Oh, is that so? But we're not even halfway done…"
"That's because we barely did anything. Seriously, why did you even come?"
"You're one to talk, when you barely did anything yourself, Setsuna."
Today went about as well as these two get along. It's almost impressive how little work got done.
It started with the album, then they went crazy about some old novels and manga, and lastly they moved on to childhood clothes Setsuna couldn't fit in anymore.
Item after item kept their hands from moving, but in return their mouths just kept going on and on.
Worst of all, they were not content with simply talking among themselves… They insisted on dragging me into their numerous "time-outs."
Even so, I didn't dare speak the truth: "Maybe it'd be faster if I did it alone."
"Still, are you sure you want to go home? Why not eat with us? Right, Haruki-kun?"
"Of course. By all means, please stay for dinner."
"Trust me, I'd love to, but I can't today."
"If you're worried about Dad and Takahiro, you can just tell them to eat out today, right? Come on, stay here a bit longer."
I can't however say "by all means" when it comes to the cruel and unusual treatment of the men in her family…
"That's not it, I have other things to take care of. I'm going to see a play tonight with Kitahara-san."
"Huh…?"
"Oh, you should've told me sooner. I would've made you a lunch box."
"I don't need that either. We have a reservation at a French restaurant after the play… Of course, I'll keep that a secret from your father and Takahiro."
The "Kitahara-san" she's talking about is of course not referring to Setsuna or me.
There is only one other person whom she'd call by the name of Kitahara.
"Anyway, that's how it is. I'll leave now."
"U-Um…"
"Yes?"
"…No, it's nothing. Thank you very much."
"Let's see each other again in your new place. See you."
"…Okay."
Perhaps she couldn't tell from the look on my face, or perhaps she simply let it pass out of consideration…
Regardless, my mother-in-law took her leave as if absolutely nothing was out of the ordinary.
Before I had known it, my own mother had also become entangled with the Ogiso household.
All the things I couldn't do, and all the things I couldn't bring myself to do, these people do with the lift of a finger.
"Now then, how about dinner?"
"…Setsuna, did you know?"
"No, not at all."
She says that, but those mischievous eyes are practically laughing at me.
Honestly, this family…
They're not bad people, of course; I really care about them. But I can't help but laugh at how our worldviews remain so different.
The strife and bonds I have been running away from all these years, they simply waltz into.
And they've actually managed to make it turn out all right.
They've handed me a resolution I couldn't even dream of attaining.
"Let's go back inside. It's starting to get cold."
"Yeah…"
All this is truly beyond my wildest dreams.
I never could have imagined spending a Sunday evening with my family.
Aimlessly watching TV without taking in any of the contents, all while the food and beer just keep coming our way.
Going from one pointless topic to the other, but then the other party would get mad when I'm not listening properly, so I'd spend hours trying to calm them.
Moments so lively, pointless, and completely unknown to me…
The thought of actually living these moments I could only dream about before.
This is the story of my dreamlike conclusion, where all wrongs have been righted…
No, this is not a dream, and it's certainly not a conclusion.
This is merely the continuation of a reality filled with joy.
